rows.title: The Chosen Few vs. Copenhagen Wolves
rows.tournament: United21 Season 57, Group A decider, BO3, online (Europe)
rows.headline: Copenhagen Wolves have a slight edge, but recent results and sparse lineup data keep it close.
rows.analysis: This is a BO3 Group A decider, not the higher-variance BO1 the market title might suggest. Both teams are unranked on HLTV; CPH’s current five (MadeInRed, Dyrod, adex, Uzman, Toshas) joined Sep 28, and its old team ranking does not measure this lineup. TCF’s active tournament lineup data is inconsistent, and HLTV has no active roster; its only two recent series were a 2-0 win over SANCTUM and 0-2 loss to Prestige. The shared-opponent comparisons are mixed: TCF beat SANCTUM by wider margins, while CPH took a map off Prestige. CPH’s recent results also include losses to ROUNDS, EAC Extra, Revise and Prestige, so the lean is modest. CPH has picked Nuke and banned Dust2; TCF picked Anubis and banned Ancient in recent event vetoes, but samples are too small for reliable three-month map rates. No named bookmaker line was verifiable for this fixture; the Kalshi book shows zero volume and wide, overlapping quotes.

rows.title: TitanFlow vs. MORROW
rows.tournament: CCT 2026 Challengers Europe Series 8, lower bracket round 3, BO3, online (Europe)
rows.headline: TitanFlow narrowly: promising current five, but too little evidence for a medal
rows.analysis: MORROW is the roster HLTV calls benched gods. TitanFlow gets a small lean after beating Noir Verse 13-9 on Anubis and 13-6 on Mirage with its current five. However, this lineup has only three documented series together: two wins and a clear loss to DONSTU. Its Honved win also came against two substitutes. MORROW's five is more established, but its last five played series produced three losses; the MAYBE win involved an opposing coach substitute and the earlier Illyrians win included a forfeited map. Today's ex-6666 walkover adds no performance evidence. Both usually ban Nuke, making veto order important; Cache and Mirage are plausible picks, with Anubis or Dust2 possible deciders. MORROW's larger Cache sample offsets some of TitanFlow's recent promise. Shared-opponent evidence is inconclusive. EGamersWorld displays 1.80 each, but no named bookmaker or independent executable quote was verified. The supplied 95-cent ask is far above my 54-cent fair value before fees. No medal: neither the data nor the price supports a strong money call.

MOUZ NXT's academy roster was rebuilt from scratch this summer: eSx/mixer joined July 10, Ay0k/Nikodeon July 23-24, opdust Aug 18 - the full five has under three weeks together, and their rank has slid from #123 (mid-Aug) to #156 while integrating. Reported book odds (~1.69 TLR/~2.00 MOUZ NXT, ~54% TLR) sit above Kalshi's ~46-47%, though unverified independently. Map veto looks roughly neutral. Roster cohesion - CS2's biggest lever - plus TLR's clearly better and stable ranking outweigh MOUZ NXT's slightly tougher recent schedule and org pedigree.

The 0.59 on Lavked reads like a pure rating-model output (GosuGamers ELO 1033 v 974, Strafe #110 v #124) and it underweights two things. First, HAVU won the Aug 18 meeting with these exact fives: Lavked forfeited Ancient at 0-8 on technical issues, then lost Nuke 13-9, so the one competitively played map went HAVU's way. Second, Nuke is Lavked's habit pick (~76% pick rate, ~36% win rate) and it is HAVU's strongest map right now, 3-1 in the last fortnight. Lavked are also 0-3 on Inferno and 0-2 on Ancient since Aug 19, and HAVU's five has been together since Jan 2025 (8Juho8 since Jun 29) against a Lavked lineup 24 days old. Against that, the Black Phoenix chain is genuine and points at Lavked. Net I make it close to even, roughly 52/48 Lavked, which makes HAVU at 0.42 the side holding the price. A value play, not a conviction play: no stand-in, no format mispricing, nothing decisive either way, hence no medal.

rows.headline: NOVAQ are 3-0 vs Rune Eaters in 2026 and rank level, yet priced as 38% underdogs
rows.analysis: Two Kazakh teams, effectively level on paper: HLTV's Aug 17 ranking has NOVAQ #87 and Rune Eaters #88, and Valve's Sep 1 list separates them by 12 points. Yet the market prices RUN at ~61.5%. The head-to-head is one-way: NOVAQ have won all three 2026 meetings 2-1 (Feb 26 MPL S2, Jun 25 LG UltraGear LAN, Jul 26 Ertis Cup grand final), the last two with the exact five they field here (neaLaN, Pump, tasman, AdreN, nyx + coach keeN). Map-level, NOVAQ have taken the Dust2 decider both times (13-10, 13-8) and hammered Mirage 13-5; RUN's edge is Inferno and Ancient. Meanwhile RUN are the ones who changed: dukefissura came in as captain/IGL on Aug 22, kumao was benched Aug 23, and they have had no coach since Jul 30 - a 12-day-old lineup priced like a settled favourite. The honest offset is that RUN are match-sharp (advanced from Group B on Aug 28, 13-5 Ancient over G2 Ares) and climbing fast (#144 in May), while NOVAQ have not played an official match since Jul 26. That caps this at a lean, not a lock - but 38% is too cheap for the team that keeps winning this fixture.

rows.tournament: Stake Ranked Episode 4 Closed Qualifier (StarLadder), Round of 16, BO3, online (EU)
rows.headline: Tougher schedule and the Sashi chain give FOKUS a hair in a genuine coin-flip BO3
rows.analysis: A coin flip on the board and close to one in reality, with a thin lean to FOKUS. Both sit in the same band (FOKUS #41, SINNERS #50) and both were 0-2'd by #212 ex-Zero Tenacity within 48 hours of each other, so the ugly recent results cancel. The separator is strength of schedule: FOKUS's 25% 30-day win rate came against MOUZ, Astralis, Heroic, Acend (#43) and Aurora - they beat Aurora 2-1 with the current five - while SINNERS' healthier ledger is built on Bushido Wildcats, Dark Tigre, MANGANESE, INOX and EAC. The one clean chain agrees: FOKUS 2-0 over Sashi (#44) on Aug 8, SINNERS 1-2 to that same Sashi in the CCT EU #5 final on Aug 2. FOKUS's July rebuild (podi for Jorko, jocab for volt) reads as a talent injection rather than a downgrade, and at seven weeks and roughly ten series it is past the danger window. SINNERS' counter-case is real - 14 months of continuity, a LORGAR S1 LAN title in April, and match sharpness against a FOKUS side that has played one series in 24 days - which is why this is 54/46 and not more.

rows.analysis: Verified grand final, BO3, online OCE, 09:00 UTC — winner takes $1,500 and the Asia-Pacific Finals slot, so no dead rubber. THUNDER lost IGL/AWPer aliStair on Aug 27 and has signed nobody; Liquipedia still lists four players plus coach viridian, with Singaporean AWPer Gratisfaction standing in. That headline scares people, but it has already been road-tested: the patched five beat Mindfreak 2-0 on Aug 28 and beat this exact Ground Zero side 2-1 on Aug 30, +21 rounds across three maps (Nuke 13-5, Inferno 12-13, Anubis 13-3). THUNDER is the better team underneath — #2 in Australia to GZ's #3, an IEM Cologne Major Stage 1 attendee, roster of Liazz/dexter/asap/TjP. The veto is GZ's structural problem: their bans run Cache then Ancient, leaving Anubis — THUNDER's 79% map over 19 maps — as the decider, exactly how Aug 30 played out. GZ's counter-case is real: stable since June 10, warm off a 2-0 over Arcade, they stole Inferno 13-12, and they won this identical LB-revenge grand final against THUNDER at the July LAN. Close, but the direct evidence and the map pool point the same way.

QUB is near-blank: about five tracked series ever, no Liquipedia team page, somnium in for qSniff around Aug 15, a 0-2 group loss to a weak LPH Gaming and a BO1 exit to Young TigeRES. Their 2-0 sweeps of Phantom Academy and EAC Rising are real, and the Phantom chain is the best case for QUB. Map pool leans Teletubisie: Nuke and Cache are their picks and QUB has zero tracked Nuke maps; QUB's Mirage is Teletubisie's soft spot, so expect a decider on Ancient or Dust II where Teletubisie is stronger. Against that, Noir Verse forfeited the winners' match to Fortress last night - a direct clash with their CCT play-in - and they have another CCT BO3 three hours after this one, so their ECL commitment is genuinely questionable. That caps the edge: I make it ~57%, barely past a book line near 55%, on an untraded Kalshi market whose asks sit far above fair on both sides.

rows.tournament: ESL Challenger League S52 Europe Cup 5, Group D decider (elimination), BO3, online EU
rows.headline: Permitta swept Azuolas 2-0 hours ago with the same five; ranking and core edge hold
rows.analysis: Verified as the Cup 5 Group D decider: csdb.gg and GosuGamers both show Permitta vs Azuolas, Aug 31 13:00 UTC, BO3, online EU — a rematch of yesterday's opener, which Permitta won 2-0 (Ancient 13-11, Mirage 16-12 OT). Both then split: Permitta swept 0-2 by WBT in the winners' match, Azuolas edged BERG 2-1. Permitta are ~#109 with an established Polish core (AdrieN, Markos, maaryy, tomiko + showk, the los kogutos five re-signed Aug 13, pako coaching); Azuolas are an unranked, brand-new all-Lithuanian roster (matyA, yakuza, MAGILA, StreakN, Uzman) with only those two series on record anywhere. The same-day, same-roster 2-0 is the best evidence available and points one way, but it was tight — 23 rounds to 29 over two maps — and a two-step chain (both Azuolas and WBT beat BERG 2-1; WBT then 2-0'd Permitta) argues Azuolas sit in the same band. Permitta's own map data is a mild drag: Ancient 25% over 90 days is their own pick, while Cache (83%) is what Azuolas ban. Fair around 62%, nowhere near the ~0.79 ask, so no medal.

rows.analysis: Two low-tier EU/CIS sides the market prices dead even (Polymarket BAKS 2.00 / Misa 1.96) despite a 60-place HLTV gap: BAKS #71 (Aug 24), Misa #131 (Aug 19). I lean BAKS narrowly. Their #71 is a career high earned BY this lineup - turbo (Mar), whisper (May), Norwi and danistzz (Jul 19-20) - so the ranking is not stale. The ugly recent line (4-13 to unranked Color, Aug 24) was a BO1 open qualifier, the noisiest sample there is; their Cup 3 losses to Fire Flux and BASEMENT BOYS were both 1-2 BO3s, and they took Virtus.pro to three maps on LAN. Misa are genuinely improving (#160 to #131 in five days) but their five is 11 days old: h0kz replaced Mertowsk1 (military service) on Aug 3, cyber replaced Ckanic on Aug 20, and their 2-0s came against Strael-Bora and ex-MANA. BO3 damps variance and favours the deeper side. This is close to a true coin flip and I am not pretending otherwise - no medal.

Bookmakers priced NEXVOID 1.54 vs Chinggis Warriors on Aug 28 against RA 1.68 vs comparable-tier The Huns, a mild echo. Against that, RA beat The Huns 13-0/13-3 on Aug 22, the best single series either side has produced. A thin lean, not an edge.

Both rosters are settled -- INFURITY's CHANKY/AwaykeN joined May 29, Teletubisie's Polish five (byali, Dycha, mASKED, POLO, Sobol) unchanged through August -- so no stand-in edge exists. GosuGamers ELO has them nearly level (1007 vs 1012, #89 vs #84 world), yet Kalshi prices Teletubisie ~0.595 mid. Teletubisie deserves the lean: better form (4-1 last five, S53 champion), the decisive H2H, and the WOPA chain. I make it roughly 56/44. That still leaves INFURITY the better-priced side at a 0.42 ask, while Teletubisie at 0.64 is worse than fair. This is a price lean on a 9-cent spread with 11 total contracts traded, not a thesis about the better team -- hence no medal and low confidence.

Legacy beat this exact Falcons side 2-0 at EWC on Aug 21 (Mirage 13-7, Dust2 13-10) and won the May CS Asia final 3-1. rows.title: Galorys vs. Fluxo W7M

rows.headline: Galorys at 39¢: a small value lean supported by the current-roster head-to-head
rows.analysis: I estimate Galorys at 42% against the 39¢ ask, a modest 3-point edge before fees. They won the only meeting with today's ten listed players, 2-0 on Anubis and Nuke, and have climbed from #122 in late August to #69. However, Fluxo remain the more likely winner: their Imperial, paiN and Back to Back comparisons are stronger, while both teams' recent 4-1 records mostly came against weaker opposition. The veto removes strengths on both sides: Galorys ban Mirage, Fluxo ban Ancient. Galorys retain a credible Nuke/Anubis route, but Fluxo can target Inferno. Fetched bookmaker snapshots disagree with my lean: Stake listed Fluxo 1.48/Galorys 2.50 and Cloudbet 1.46/2.55, implying roughly 36-37% for Galorys after margin removal; HLTV's displayed 1.55/2.36 pair implies about 40%. Neither lineup is newly assembled, and no verified stand-in or hidden disruption supports a medal. Current listings and the newer event report confirm BO3, superseding an older BO1 announcement. This is a fragile underdog value call, with substantial outright loss risk.

rows.headline: maybe offers the better relative price, but unresolved lineup risk limits conviction
rows.analysis: The required selection is maybe at 42%, although its 47c ask implies a negative 5c expected return per share before fees. Noir Verse's 77c ask is substantially further above my valuation. Fonbet and Leon quote Noir Verse 1.65/maybe 2.10, implying 44% for maybe after removing margin; Bitel shows 1.80/1.90, implying 48.6%. No sharp-book quote was verified. I reduce those estimates for maybe's instability: m4d4ra replaced zogeN on Oct 16, a missing fifth caused a map forfeit on Oct 18, and coach BORSCHETSKIY replaced edixenn on Oct 20. Today's listed five includes edixenn, but his return lacks match-day confirmation. Both teams are 1-4 across their last five HLTV-listed series. maybe's latest H2H sweep and Ryvex win offer resistance, but both used zogeN; Ryvex also fielded a different five against Noir Verse. Noir Verse has the broader map record and steadier lineup, offset by several recent losses to lower-ranked opposition. Mixed chains and uncertain vetoes justify no medal. The 13:00 UTC schedule is corroborated by match trackers; no match-specific HLTV listing was found and Liquipedia's page fetch was blocked.

rows.analysis: Both rosters are confirmed and stable, so this is a straight strength question. Sashi (acoR, Cabbi, Anlelele, Zyphon, MistR, together since 20 Jul) sit #48 with a CCT Europe S5 title and a 2-1 win over Virtus.pro at the EWC open qualifier. Metizport (stanislaw, forsyy, F1KU, Plopski, MaiL09, coach vinS) are #75 but the hottest team in the match: #127 in mid-June, #90 on 19 Aug, +37 Elo in 30 days, an ESL Challenger League Europe Cup #4 title over OG, and 8-2 in their last ten maps-series. Second, Nuke is Lavked's habit pick (~76% pick rate, ~36% win rate) and it is HAVU's strongest map right now, 3-1 in the last fortnight. Against that, the Black Phoenix chain is genuine and points at Lavked. Net I make it close to even, roughly 52/48 Lavked, which makes HAVU at 0.42 the side holding the price. A value play, not a conviction play: no stand-in, no format mispricing, nothing decisive either way, hence no medal.

rows.headline: Tougher schedule and the Sashi chain give FOKUS a hair in a genuine coin-flip BO3
rows.analysis: A coin flip on the board and close to one in reality, with a thin lean to FOKUS. Both sit in the same band (FOKUS #41, SINNERS #50) and both were 0-2'd by #212 ex-Zero Tenacity within 48 hours of each other, so the ugly recent results cancel. The separator is strength of schedule: FOKUS's 25% 30-day win rate came against MOUZ, Astralis, Heroic, Acend (#43) and Aurora - they beat Aurora 2-1 with the current five - while SINNERS' healthier ledger is built on Bushido Wildcats, Dark Tigre, MANGANESE, INOX and EAC. The one clean chain agrees: FOKUS 2-0 over Sashi (#44) on Aug 8, SINNERS 1-2 to that same Sashi in the CCT EU #5 final on Aug 2. FOKUS's July rebuild (podi for Jorko, jocab for volt) reads as a talent injection rather than a downgrade, and at seven weeks and roughly ten series it is past the danger window. SINNERS' counter-case is real - 14 months of continuity, a LORGAR S1 LAN title in April, and match sharpness against a FOKUS side that has played one series in 24 days - which is why this is 54/46 and not more.

GZ's counter-case is real: stable since June 10, warm off a 2-0 over Arcade, they stole Inferno 13-12, and they won this identical LB-revenge grand final against THUNDER at the July LAN. The cleanest read is a shared opponent one day apart: EMPIRE upset Zomblers 2-1 on Aug 26 (Dust2 13-10, Nuke 13-7), then Chicken Coop dismantled that same EMPIRE 2-0 on Aug 27, 13-0 on Dust2 and 13-6 on Inferno. Same event, same servers, same rosters; CC were +20 net rounds where Zomblers were -7. Behind it sits a class gap Dust2.us states plainly: CC are the only top-ten NA side in this field besides Voca and Marsborne, ~#95 HLTV to Zomblers' ~#190, on a stable five that won ESEA S57 and FRAG TAP Reloaded and peaked #64 in July. Zomblers carry a rookie rifler (man327, no prior HLTV maps) five weeks into the lineup after an acrimonious Zoker split, plus a head coach promoted July 1. Veto compounds it: CC ban Inferno, which is Zomblers' pick and their only map won against EMPIRE, then pick Dust2, which Zomblers lost. BO3 damps the variance that would otherwise rescue the underdog. 0.72 against a 0.62 mid.

rows.analysis: ECL S52 SA Cup 1, lower-bracket elimination BO3, online. ShindeN are the better-rated side (Valve Americas #15 vs #22) with the more settled team: the same five since Feb 14 and two 2026 titles (Aorus League Latam, Thunderpick SA #1). They lead the H2H 2-1 and 5-3 on maps, and all three meetings came with this identical ShindeN five, while Isurus fielded a different fifth each time. Isurus are genuinely in form -- three straight 2-1 elimination wins over paiN Academy, Keyd Stars and Turma do Pagode -- but the same tape shows a gaping Ancient hole: 3-13, 2-13, 6-13 in this event, and opponents keep picking it into them. Isurus also carry the newer pieces: rzk since ~early July (still absent from Liquipedia's roster page) and coach pino installed in Week 34, mid-tournament. Transitive chains lean ShindeN -- they beat Imperial 3-1 in a BO5 and swept ex-MIBR 13-9/13-3, where Isurus lost 0-2 to both Imperial and MIBR Academy -- though UNO MILLE cuts the other way. Fair around 60% against a 57% market: a real but thin lean, so no medal.

rows.analysis: Tier-4 NA online BO3, ECL S52 NA Cup 1 lower-bracket elimination (loser 5th-6th; winner still alive for the $8k and a Regional Final seat). The two are dead level on Valve's Americas list — EMPIRE #58/639, Overtake #59/631 — and have never met. In-event, Overtake beat Villainous (#39) 2-1 and NuTorious (#37) 2-1, then lost 1-2 to top seed Voca (#16), winning a map and losing Dust II 13-10. EMPIRE upset Zomblers (#44) 2-1, were 0-2'd by Chicken Coop (#22) including a 13-0 on Dust II, then ground out New Legends and Iowa Stormboar 2-1 each. Overtake's map differential (net 0 over 9) against stiffer opposition is the better line, though EMPIRE's 13-0 outlier flatters it. Veto is the one asymmetry: Nuke has not appeared in any of Overtake's three series (near-certain permaban) while EMPIRE has had Nuke available in all four of theirs and is 2-1 on it — their best map likely gets removed. Both field an unannounced fifth (corim for Overtake, ayaneuu for EMPIRE), so neither ranking measures the team that actually plays. Fair lands ~0.61 — right on the ask, so no medal.

rows.title: INFURITY Gaming vs. Teletubisie
rows.tournament: United21 Season 54, upper-bracket semifinal, BO3, online (EU), C-tier $10k
rows.headline: Near-identical ELO and a 1-1 H2H make 0.42 the better-priced side in a thin market
rows.analysis: Two unranked tier-3 sides who have met twice in three weeks with these exact rosters: INFURITY won 2-1 on Aug 11 (S53 UB SF), Teletubisie won 2-0 on Aug 14 (S53 LB Final) to eliminate them, then took the title. Both rosters are settled -- INFURITY's CHANKY/AwaykeN joined May 29, Teletubisie's Polish five (byali, Dycha, mASKED, POLO, Sobol) unchanged through August -- so no stand-in edge exists. GosuGamers ELO has them nearly level (1007 vs 1012, #89 vs #84 world), yet Kalshi prices Teletubisie ~0.595 mid. Teletubisie deserves the lean: better form (4-1 last five, S53 champion), the decisive H2H, and the WOPA chain. I make it roughly 56/44. That still leaves INFURITY the better-priced side at a 0.42 ask, while Teletubisie at 0.64 is worse than fair. This is a price lean on a 9-cent spread with 11 total contracts traded, not a thesis about the better team -- hence no medal and low confidence.

rows.analysis: Group A lower-bracket semifinal, BO3 LAN in Copenhagen; the loser is eliminated. The market is a true pick'em (Polymarket G2 2.00 / NAVI 1.96) despite a clear divergence in trajectory. NAVI sat #2 from April to July and have fallen to #8: 9th at EWC after a 0-2 exit to Legacy with consecutive 2-10 opening halves, then a 1-2 reverse-sweep loss to M80 opening this event. G2 beat that same M80 side at EWC, went unbeaten through their EWC group, beat Astralis 2-1 in the Ro16 and lost only to FURIA 1-2 in the quarters; here they beat Aurora 2-0 and lost only to #1 Spirit. G2 also lead the 2026 H2H 2-1, taking the last two, including June's Major decider where NAVI coughed up a 12-8 Inferno lead. Underneath, NAVI is unstable: Aleksib is at 0.86 over three months (0.70 in the Legacy loss), insiders report NAVI targeted Alex666 to replace him, and a roster change before September was priced near 78%. Counterweight: June's map swap deleted Overpass, G2's best map at 81.8%, and freed NAVI's permaban, and NAVI are 3-0 on Dust2 versus G2 this year. Small but real lean to G2.

rows.analysis: Online BO3, Group C opener of the Logitech G Play Connect closed qualifier (feeds a $100k Warsaw LAN). Rankings favour OG (#61 vs #78, Aug 24) yet the market has EF at ~54% on both Kalshi and Polymarket (1.82 vs 2.17) — it has already absorbed the news, which is why this is ungraded. The news is real: on Aug 23 EF benched br0 (0.93 over 21 maps) for soulfly, an ex-Aurora rifler with a 1.01 rating, an EPL S23 final and an IEM Cologne Major semi behind him, and made jottAAA permanent. In soulfly's debut the next day, #78 EF beat #31 100 Thieves 2-1 to reach the IEM Beijing closed qualifier, taking the decider 13-10 from 6-10 down. EF also won European Pro League S8 on Jul 24 (3-2 over 1win). OG went 3-1 in ESL Challenger League S52 Cup 4 but lost the final 1-2 to #90 Metizport, and were swept 0-2 by BC.Game at the EWC open qualifier. I make EF ~57%, a shade above 54c; the offset is that OG's cadiaN-led five is unchanged since May 19 while EF's has one BO3 together.

Against that: INOX re-signed gooddeph on Aug 14, restoring the founding five, and the #62-to-#81 slide was earned with notineki standing in; they are 4-2 since, with 13-4/13-6/13-7 scorelines. Chains are mixed — SINNERS and Virtus.pro favour Sashi, ex-RUSTEC favours INOX. Veto is near-symmetric: Sashi 4-1 on Cache but 1-4 on Dust II; INOX 4-1 on Inferno. rows.analysis: Both are playoff invites who won their R16, and the two ranking systems agree they are near-identical: HLTV #64 Nemiga vs #68 Phantom, Valve 1134 vs 1130. The market still makes Nemiga a small favourite, which looks like brand anchoring on an org that won CCT EU S1, NODWIN Clutch 7, BC.Game Masters S1 and A1 S11 earlier in 2026 with a different five. That five is gone: sowalio was benched Aug 15 for Xant3r, and robo has been a 'trial basis' stand-in IGL since Jul 17. The current lineup went 1-3 at the GLuck Moscow closed qualifier this week, losing to 1win (Anubis 14-16, D2 6-13), ex-RUBY, and Nuclear TigeRES on Aug 28 to go out. Phantom has been settled since Jul 6, has the best statistical player on the server in nicoodoz (1.3 K/D, 79.6 ADR), and banning Dust2 in veto removes the map Nemiga just used to bury Black Phoenix 13-4. At 0.49 ask on a coin-flip matchup, Phantom is the value side.

rows.analysis: Both are tier-4 EU sides and the market has them dead level, but the evidence isn't. Since Aug 14 Honvéd have one real win in seven played series -- 0-2 to INOX, 0-2 to Inner Circle Academy, 0-2 to Bushido Wildcats, 0-2 to ex-Zero Tenacity, 1-2 to Falcons Force -- and that lone win was over Noir Verse. Then the schedule -- Honvéd play a full BO3 vs SPARTA at 16:00 CEST, three hours before this one; NV haven't played since Aug 23. Against that: Honvéd 2-0'd them 11 days ago, and NV lost fostar on Aug 24 and show four players on HLTV. rows.headline: NAVI Junior #147 with a settled roster, priced 50/50 vs unranked, scrambled Dark Moon
rows.analysis: ESEA Advanced S58 Europe regular season is a 14-match round robin of BO1s (Liquipedia), so variance is high and there is no veto edge - six bans, one map left. Under that, take the better team at a coin-flip price. NAVI Junior sit HLTV ~#147 with 914.1 Valve points and have fielded the same five - kodak, Yoki, FAZERY, MahaR, skizzyee under coach snatchie - since 31 Mar 2026, with an academy structure behind them. Their BO1 record is the tell: 13-5 BRUTE, 13-5 LEO, 13-2 MOUZ NXT on LAN at Urban Riga Open #6 in July. Dark Moon are unranked on HLTV, 669.2 Valve points, and Valve's 17 Aug snapshot registers only four players (d3j4vy, keiyon, Maison, ri0dayungog) while the lineup actually being fielded is Bak0, crewwwl, d3j4vy, keiyon, rui - Bak0 has no HLTV or Liquipedia footprint at all. They have dropped their recent ESEA BO1s to Arch, SANGAL 1XALTERS, eSuba and banda chuya, and lost an open-qualifier R16 12-13 to gribo4ki in July. Shared opponent eSuba points the same way. Fair around 0.64; 0.53 is the buy.

rows.headline: Legacy at 0.39 undersells a side that beat this exact Falcons five 2-0 eight days ago
rows.analysis: Group B UB semi, BO3, Copenhagen studio LAN; loser drops to lower bracket, so neither is eliminated. Both fives confirmed unchanged: Falcons karrigan/NiKo/m0NESY/TeSeS/kyousuke (zonic coach); Legacy arT/dumau/latto/n1ssim/try, with try in since Jul 11. Legacy beat this exact Falcons side 2-0 at EWC on Aug 21 (Mirage 13-7, Dust2 13-10) and won the May CS Asia final 3-1. Since Jul 11 Legacy are 5-2 with wins over NAVI, Falcons, FURIA and FUT; Falcons have not beaten a top-8 team since the Jun 21 Major final and needed three maps against #32 Lynn Vision on Aug 27, losing their own Ancient pick. HLTV still reads #2 vs #7; Valve VRS has them far closer. The veto pushes back: Falcons will now ban Mirage (Legacy near-perfect there) and can pick Nuke, Legacy's weakest map, and Falcons had five days' rest to Legacy's EWC-to-Copenhagen grind. Net I make Falcons ~57%, so Legacy at 0.39 is about four points of value — a price play, not a claim they are favourites.
